user.title: Microsoft Family Safety
user.description: Configure the integration. After Submit, Home Assistant opens the Microsoft sign-in through a temporary authentication proxy. Sign in with the parent account and answer **Yes** to "Stay signed in?": that is what keeps the Family session valid for about a year instead of a few hours. If Home Assistant is not reachable over HTTPS, local HTTP can be explicitly enabled for testing; Microsoft credentials are then not transport-encrypted on the local network.

data.allow_insecure_http_auth: Allow insecure local HTTP authentication (testing only)

data_description.platforms: Windows, Xbox, Mobile: one lock switch per ticked platform. Ticking Xbox also turns on Xbox play time and the Xbox lock, which need the Microsoft web session (some accounts must renew it with a sign-in every 24 hours). Leave Xbox unticked if the children have no Xbox: the integration then runs on the mobile token only, with a shorter sign-in.

auth.title: Manual Microsoft Family Safety authentication
auth.description:
Home Assistant could not use the secure browser-assisted login because no HTTPS Home Assistant URL is configured. Open this Microsoft URL, sign in, and paste the complete resulting redirect URL here:

{auth_url}

reauth_confirm.title: Reauthenticate Microsoft Family Safety
reauth_confirm.description: The stored Microsoft sign-in is incomplete, expired, or revoked. Continue to run the complete sign-in again and renew both the mobile refresh token and the Family web session.

reauth_full_confirm.title: Reauthenticate Microsoft Family Safety
reauth_full_confirm.description: The stored Microsoft authentication is incomplete, expired, or revoked. Continue to sign in again; answer **Yes** to "Stay signed in?" so the renewed session lasts. If this Home Assistant instance is only reachable over a private local HTTP URL, enable the local HTTP test option below.

data.allow_insecure_http_auth: Allow insecure local HTTP authentication (testing only)

reauth_success.title: Microsoft Family Safety sign-in completed
reauth_success.description: Microsoft authentication completed successfully and the new credentials are ready to be saved. Select Submit to finish the reauthentication.

check_mobile_proxy.title: Microsoft sign-in
check_mobile_proxy.description:
Sign in with the Microsoft account that manages the family, and answer **Yes** when Microsoft asks "Stay signed in?". Keep the opened authentication window open: after the visible sign-in completes, Home Assistant switches to a waiting screen while the Family session and the mobile token are established.

A passkey can't be used here, because the sign-in runs through Home Assistant's address rather than Microsoft's: if Microsoft offers one, choose **Sign in another way** and use your password or a code.

check_proxy.title: Microsoft Family web session
check_proxy.description:
**Sign in in the window that just opened**, with the Microsoft account that manages the family, and answer **Yes** to "Stay signed in?".

Then come back here and **wait**: this dialog continues on its own, which can take up to about a minute after the sign-in. Do not press *Open website* again unless the Microsoft window never opened or was closed before you signed in.

A passkey can't be used here, because the sign-in runs through Home Assistant's address rather than Microsoft's: if Microsoft offers one, choose **Sign in another way** and use your password or a code.

auth_success.title: Microsoft Family Safety sign-in completed
auth_success.description: Microsoft sign-in completed: the Family web session and the mobile refresh token are both ready. Select Continue to create the integration.

error.no_redirect_url: Please enter a valid redirect URL.

error.native_http_not_local: Insecure HTTP authentication is allowed only through localhost, .local, or a private/local IP address.

data.xbox_link: Link the Xbox Family Settings sign-in

data_description.platforms: Windows, Xbox, Mobile: one lock switch per ticked platform. Ticking Xbox also turns on Xbox play time and the Xbox lock, which need the Microsoft web session (some accounts must renew it with a sign-in every 24 hours). Leave Xbox unticked if the children have no Xbox: the integration then runs on the mobile token only, with a shorter sign-in.
data_description.allowed_users: Leave empty to let every user use the buttons and settings (default). As soon as users are ticked, only they and the administrators can: a child's non-administrator account is refused on every button, switch, limit and time window, and on the microsoft_family_safety actions. Automations and scripts run by Home Assistant are not affected. Give the child a non-administrator account: an administrator can change this option.
data_description.xbox_link: Xbox limits, the Xbox lock and Xbox play time then come from the Xbox Family Settings app's service, on their own sign-in, without the web session. Only with Xbox ticked. Usually linked automatically after a sign-in; tick this if the Connection sensor shows xbox_family: not_linked.

xbox_link_manual.title: Link Xbox Family Settings
xbox_link_manual.description:
1. Open [this Microsoft sign-in]({url}) and sign in with the parent account you use in the Xbox Family Settings app.
2. You end up on a blank page whose address starts with `{redirect_prefix}`. Copy that whole address and paste it below within a few minutes.

error.xbox_link_failed: Microsoft did not accept that address. Sign in again with the new link and paste the address straight away.

progress.xbox_link: Open [this Microsoft sign-in]({url}) and sign in with the parent account you use in the Xbox Family Settings app. Once Microsoft has accepted the sign-in, the window shows "Sign-in received" and can be closed; this step then continues on its own, with nothing to copy. If the sign-in does not finish within 10 minutes, you can paste the address instead. A passkey can't be used here, because the sign-in runs through Home Assistant's address rather than Microsoft's: if Microsoft offers one, choose **Sign in another way** and use your password or a code.

add_time_bonus.name: Add Extra Time
add_time_bonus.description: Give a child extra time on the Xbox or on Windows, for some minutes or until a time. Xbox: through the Xbox Family Settings service, which needs the Xbox Family Settings sign-in linked. Windows: through the Family Safety mobile API. Refused while the platform is locked, unless Replace lock is on. Fails when Microsoft does not confirm the extra time, or when the platform stays locked. Can answer with added, until and replaced_lock.

minutes.name: Minutes
minutes.description: Extra time from now, 1 to 1440 minutes. Give this or until.

until.name: Until
until.description: When the extra time ends, instead of minutes (at most 24 hours from now).

replace_lock.name: Replace lock
replace_lock.description: Microsoft keeps one override per platform, so extra time replaces a lock. Off (default): refused while the platform is locked, by this integration or by a parent. On: the lock is replaced by the extra time.

cancel_time_bonus.name: Cancel Extra Time
cancel_time_bonus.description: Cancel the extra time in force on a child's Xbox or Windows. Only extra time is cancelled: fails while the platform is locked (a lock is never lifted), and does nothing when no extra time is in force. Can answer with cancelled and reason or lock_in_force.

pause_app.name: Pause App
pause_app.description: Block Windows or Xbox apps of a child for now. Each app's policy (its daily time limit, or none) is read from Microsoft and saved before its first pause, and kept while it is blocked; resume_app puts it back. Apps already blocked, or whose policy cannot be read, are not paused. A repeat pause keeps the first saved state, also after a restart; an app whose limit a parent changed since is left as it is. Answers with the apps paused, changed by a parent, skipped and failed; fails when every app failed.

resume_app.name: Resume App
resume_app.description: Unblock apps pause_app blocked, putting back the time limit each had before (or none), and forget their saved state. Without apps, every paused app of the child. An app someone unblocked or changed in the meantime is left as it is. Answers with the apps resumed, released, changed by a parent, skipped and failed; fails when every app failed.
